business_problem: Elisity's IdentityGraph could discover assets and basic identity signals but lacked detailed threat, vulnerability, and component information needed to build effective security segmentation policies.
solution_summary: Elisity integrated Armis from ServiceNow with its IdentityGraph and control plane to enrich identity-based network security with AI-powered asset intelligence. Through the Armis API, Elisity receives risk scores, vulnerability details, serial numbers, firmware versions, and industrial-control context, then combines those attributes with identity signals to group assets and build segmentation policies. Elisity processes the information in its backend and uses large language models to map trends in the cyber-threat landscape and help refine policies for customer environments. The integration is bidirectional: Armis data informs Elisity policy, and Elisity shares policy-enforcement status back to Armis so customers can identify assets that are or are not protected. The source describes APIs and backend processing but does not name model or hosting products.
